subject: Chemistry
questionText: An unknown organic compound X (C₈H₈O) gives a positive 2,4-DNP test forming an orange precipitate. Compound X reduces Tollens' reagent to form a silver mirror and gives a positive Iodoform test yielding yellow CHI₃ ↓. Upon treatment with dilute NaOH, compound X undergoes a self-condensation reaction. What is the structural identity of X?

options.explanation: Acetophenone is a ketone and does NOT reduce Tollens' reagent to form a silver mirror.
Lacks α-hydrogens on the aldehyde carbon to undergo self-condensation aldol reaction.

1. Positive 2,4-DNP test ⟹ X is an Aldehyde or Ketone. 2. Reduces Tollens' reagent ⟹ X MUST be an ALDEHYDE (RCHO), eliminating Acetophenone. 3. Positive Iodoform test and Aldol condensation ⟹ 2-Phenylacetaldehyde (C₆H₅CH₂CHO) contains α-hydrogens, undergoes Aldol, and reduces Tollens' reagent. Therefore, Option C is the intended aldehyde.
Aromatic aldehyde lacking α-hydrogens for aldol self-condensation.

solutionExplanation:
1. Positive 2,4-DNP test ⟹ X is an Aldehyde or Ketone.
2. Reduces Tollens' reagent ⟹ X MUST be an ALDEHYDE (RCHO). This eliminates Acetophenone (a ketone).
3. 2-Phenylacetaldehyde (C₆H₅CH₂CHO) contains α-hydrogens, undergoes aldol self-condensation, and reduces Tollens' reagent.
hints: Tollens' reduction rules out ketones; aldol requires α-hydrogens.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: What is the major organic product obtained when Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) is reacted with Formaldehyde (HCHO) in the presence of concentrated 50% NaOH solution (Crossed Cannizzaro Reaction)?

options.explanation: In a Crossed Cannizzaro reaction between Benzaldehyde and Formaldehyde, nucleophilic addition of OH⁻ occurs preferentially at the more electrophilic, less sterically hindered formaldehyde carbon (HCHO). Hydride transfer from the formal adduct reduces Benzaldehyde to Benzyl Alcohol (C₆H₅CH₂OH), while Formaldehyde is oxidized to Sodium Formate (HCOONa).
Formaldehyde is oxidized preferentially due to faster nucleophilic attack and hydride release.
Disproportionation requires one oxidation product (carboxylate) and one reduction product (alcohol).
Both cannot be oxidized without a corresponding reduction.

solutionExplanation: In a Crossed Cannizzaro reaction between Benzaldehyde and Formaldehyde, nucleophilic addition of OH⁻ occurs preferentially at the more electrophilic, less sterically hindered formaldehyde carbon (HCHO). Hydride transfer from the formal adduct reduces Benzaldehyde to Benzyl Alcohol (C₆H₅CH₂OH), while Formaldehyde is oxidized to Sodium Formate (HCOONa).
hints: Formaldehyde is more electrophilic and forms the hydride-donor adduct, getting oxidized to formate.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: An ester E (C₄H₈O₂) is treated with 1 equivalent of Diisobutylaluminium hydride (DIBAL-H) in dry toluene at -78°C, followed by aqueous workup. What organic products are formed from this selective reduction?

options.explanation: Complete reduction to alcohol occurs with LiAlH₄, not DIBAL-H at -78°C.
DIBAL-H at low temperatures (-78°C) selectively reduces esters (RCOOR') to Aldehydes (RCHO) and Alcohols (R'OH) without reducing the formed aldehyde further to a primary alcohol.
Reduction does not form carboxylic acids.
Incorrect reaction pathway.

solutionExplanation: DIBAL-H at low temperatures (-78°C) selectively reduces esters (RCOOR') to Aldehydes (RCHO) and Alcohols (R'OH) without reducing the formed aldehyde further to a primary alcohol.
hints: DIBAL-H at -78°C stops reduction of esters cleanly at the aldehyde stage.

subject: Chemistry
questionText:
Arrange the following carboxylic acids in order of INCREASING Acidic Strength (lowest acidity to highest acidity):

1. Acetic Acid (CH₃COOH)
2. Formic Acid (HCOOH)
3. Fluoroacetic Acid (FCH₂COOH)
4. Trichloroacetic Acid (CCl₃COOH)

options.explanation: • Electron-donating +I groups (-CH₃ in Acetic acid) destabilize carboxylate, decreasing acidity (CH₃COOH < HCOOH). • Electron-withdrawing -I groups (-F, -Cl) stabilize carboxylate, increasing acidity. • -F is more electronegative than -Cl, so FCH₂COOH > HCOOH. • Three -Cl groups (CCl₃COOH) exert a massive -I effect, making it the strongest acid. Increasing acidity order: CH₃COOH (1) < HCOOH (2) < FCH₂COOH (3) < CCl₃COOH (4).
Acetic acid is weaker than Formic acid.
Decreasing order instead of increasing.
Fluoroacetic acid is stronger than Formic acid.

solutionExplanation:
• Electron-donating +I groups (-CH₃ in Acetic acid) destabilize carboxylate, decreasing acidity (CH₃COOH < HCOOH).
• Electron-withdrawing -I groups (-F, -Cl) stabilize carboxylate, increasing acidity.
• -F is more electronegative than -Cl, so FCH₂COOH > HCOOH.
• Three -Cl groups (CCl₃COOH) exert a massive -I effect, making it the strongest acid.
Increasing acidity order: CH₃COOH (1) < HCOOH (2) < FCH₂COOH (3) < CCl₃COOH (4).
hints: +I decreases acidity; -I strongly increases acidity.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: When Propanoic Acid (CH₃CH₂COOH) is treated with Red Phosphorus and Br₂ followed by addition of water (Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky / HVZ Reaction), what is the structural formula of the final organic product?

options.explanation: Acid bromide intermediate is hydrolyzed by water back to carboxylic acid.

The HVZ reaction selectively halogenates the α-carbon of carboxylic acids possessing α-hydrogens. Propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH) has 2 α-hydrogens at C-2. Treatment with Red P / Br₂ ──► H₂O yields 2-Bromopropanoic acid (CH₃CH(Br)COOH).
Halogenation occurs strictly at the α-carbon (C-2), not the β-carbon (C-3).
Monobromination at the α-position is the primary product with 1 eq Br₂.

solutionExplanation: The HVZ reaction selectively halogenates the α-carbon of carboxylic acids possessing α-hydrogens. Propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH) has 2 α-hydrogens at C-2. Treatment with Red P / Br₂ ──► H₂O yields 2-Bromopropanoic acid (CH₃CH(Br)COOH).
hints: HVZ selectively substitutes bromine onto the α-carbon adjacent to -COOH.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following acid derivatives undergoes nucleophilic acyl substitution at the FASTEST intrinsic rate when reacted with water (H₂O)?

options.explanation: Least reactive due to strong resonance and poor NH₂⁻ leaving group.
Esters are less reactive than acyl chlorides and anhydrides.
Reactive, but slower than acyl chlorides.

Nucleophilic acyl substitution reactivity depends on leaving group stability (Cl⁻ > RCOO⁻ > RO⁻ > NH₂⁻) and carbonyl electrophilicity. Acetyl Chloride (CH₃COCl) contains the best leaving group (Cl⁻) and highest carbonyl δ+ charge, reacting violently with water at room temperature.

solutionExplanation: Nucleophilic acyl substitution reactivity depends on leaving group stability (Cl⁻ > RCOO⁻ > RO⁻ > NH₂⁻) and carbonyl electrophilicity. Acetyl Chloride (CH₃COCl) contains the best leaving group (Cl⁻) and highest carbonyl δ+ charge, reacting violently with water at room temperature.
hints: Chloride ion is the weakest base and best leaving group among acid derivatives.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: What is the major product obtained when Pentan-3-one (CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃) is treated with Hydrazine (NH₂NH₂) followed by heating with KOH in Ethylene Glycol solvent at 180°C (Wolff-Kishner Reduction)?

options.explanation: Pentan-3-ol is the product of NaBH₄ reduction, not deoxygenation.
The Wolff-Kishner Reduction (NH₂NH₂ / KOH, ethylene glycol, Δ) completely deoxygenates carbonyl groups (>C=O) into methylene groups (>CH₂). Pentan-3-one is reduced directly to n-Pentane.
Elimination product, not the primary deoxygenation product.
Oxidation product, not reduction.

solutionExplanation: The Wolff-Kishner Reduction (NH₂NH₂ / KOH, ethylene glycol, Δ) completely deoxygenates carbonyl groups (>C=O) into methylene groups (>CH₂). Pentan-3-one is reduced directly to n-Pentane.
hints: Wolff-Kishner converts >C=O directly into >CH₂ (hydrocarbon).

subject: Chemistry
questionText: A student mixes Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO) and Propanal (CH₃CH₂CHO) in dilute NaOH solution and heats the mixture (Claisen-Schmidt Crossed Aldol). What is the IUPAC name of the major dehydrated cross-aldol condensation product?

options.explanation: 1. Enolate generation occurs at the α-carbon of Propanal: CH₃-C̄H-CHO. 2. Enolate attacks Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO): C₆H₅CHO + CH₃CH₂CHO ──► C₆H₅-CH(OH)-CH(CH₃)-CHO. 3. Dehydration (-H₂O) yields C₆H₅-CH=C(CH₃)-CHO (2-Methyl-3-phenylprop-2-enal).
Cinnamaldehyde is formed from Benzaldehyde + Acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO), not Propanal.
Requires acetophenone as the reactant.
Incorrect condensation architecture.

solutionExplanation:
1. Enolate generation occurs at the α-carbon of Propanal: CH₃-C̄H-CHO.
2. Enolate attacks Benzaldehyde (C₆H₅CHO): C₆H₅CHO + CH₃CH₂CHO ──► C₆H₅-CH(OH)-CH(CH₃)-CHO.
3. Dehydration (-H₂O) yields C₆H₅-CH=C(CH₃)-CHO (2-Methyl-3-phenylprop-2-enal).
hints: The α-carbon of propanal is C-2 (bearing the methyl branch).

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Why does Semicarbazide (H₂N⁽¹⁾-NH-CO-NH₂⁽²⁾) react with aldehydes to form semicarbazones using ONLY the NH₂⁽¹⁾ group, while the NH₂⁽²⁾ group remains completely unreactive?

options.text: NH₂⁽²⁾ is sterically blocked by two phenyl rings.
options.explanation: There are no phenyl rings in semicarbazide.

options.text: Lone pair electrons on NH₂⁽²⁾ are delocalized into the adjacent carbonyl group via resonance (H₂N-C(=O)-NH₂ ⟷ H₂N-C(O⁻)=NH₂⁺), making them non-nucleophilic.
options.explanation: Semicarbazide contains two terminal amino groups. The electrons on NH₂⁽²⁾ are conjugated with the carbonyl C=O group through resonance and are delocalized, making them non-nucleophilic. The NH₂⁽¹⁾ group attached to -NH- is isolated from the carbonyl, retaining its localized lone pair to act as a strong nucleophile.
NH₂ groups are basic/nucleophilic, not acidic.

options.text: NH₂⁽²⁾ undergoes immediate oxidation to N₂ gas.
options.explanation: Oxidation to N₂ does not occur in standard condensation.

solutionExplanation: Semicarbazide contains two terminal amino groups. The electrons on NH₂⁽²⁾ are conjugated with the carbonyl C=O group through resonance and are delocalized, making them non-nucleophilic. The NH₂⁽¹⁾ group attached to -NH- is isolated from the carbonyl, retaining its localized lone pair to act as a strong nucleophile.
hints: Amide resonance delocalizes the lone pair of the NH₂ group directly attached to C=O.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: What organic acid is produced when a Grignard reagent, Methylmagnesium bromide (CH₃MgBr), is reacted with Solid Carbon Dioxide (Dry Ice) in dry ether, followed by acidic hydrolysis (H₃O⁺)?

options.explanation: Formic acid contains 1 carbon; CH₃MgBr + CO₂ adds a 2nd carbon.
1. Nucleophilic attack of CH₃⁻ from Grignard onto electrophilic CO₂: CH₃MgBr + O=C=O ──► CH₃-COO⁻ MgBr⁺. 2. Acidic hydrolysis yields Acetic Acid (CH₃COOH) + Mg(OH)Br.
Propanoic acid requires Ethylmagnesium bromide.
Dicarboxylic acid not formed from monomagnesium Grignard.

solutionExplanation:
1. Nucleophilic attack of CH₃⁻ from Grignard onto electrophilic CO₂: CH₃MgBr + O=C=O ──► CH₃-COO⁻ MgBr⁺.
2. Acidic hydrolysis yields Acetic Acid (CH₃COOH) + Mg(OH)Br.
hints: Grignard carbonation adds 1 carbon to the alkyl group of the Grignard reagent.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following aldehydes/ketones will undergo a CANNIZZARO REACTION when treated with concentrated 50% NaOH solution? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Lacks α-hydrogens, undergoes Cannizzaro to methanol + formate.
Lacks α-hydrogens, undergoes Cannizzaro to benzyl alcohol + benzoate.
Lacks α-hydrogens, undergoes Cannizzaro to neopentyl alcohol + pivalate.
Possesses 3 α-hydrogens and undergoes Aldol condensation instead.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: HCHO, C₆H₅CHO, and (CH₃)₃C-CHO LACK α-hydrogens and undergo self-redox Cannizzaro reactions in 50% NaOH.
• D is incorrect: Acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO) HAS 3 α-hydrogens and undergoes Aldol Condensation instead!
hints: Cannizzaro strictly requires the absence of α-hydrogens.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the correct statements regarding Tollens' and Fehling's diagnostic tests: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Tollens' reagent ([Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺) oxidizes both aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes to carboxylates, forming a silver mirror (Ag⁰ ↓).
options.explanation: Universal aldehyde oxidation reagent.

options.text: Fehling's solution (Cu²⁺ tartrate complex) oxidizes ALIPHATIC aldehydes to give a red precipitate of Cu₂O ↓.
options.explanation: Oxidizes aliphatic aldehydes.

options.text: Aromatic aldehydes like Benzaldehyde reduce Tollens' reagent but FAIL to reduce Fehling's solution.
options.explanation: Aromatic aldehydes fail Fehling's test due to weaker electrophilicity.

options.text: Ketones readily reduce both Tollens' and Fehling's reagents under mild conditions.
options.explanation: Ketones are resistant to mild oxidation and give negative Tollens' and Fehling's tests.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Tollens' oxidizes aliphatic/aromatic aldehydes; Fehling's oxidizes only aliphatic aldehydes (benzaldehyde fails Fehling's).
• D is incorrect: Simple ketones are resistant to oxidation and give negative tests for both Tollens' and Fehling's.
hints: Aromatic aldehydes reduce Tollens' but fail Fehling's.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following reagents can be used to perform a DEOXYGENATION REDUCTION of a carbonyl group (>C=O ──► >CH₂)? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Acidic deoxygenation of carbonyls to methylene groups.

options.text: NH₂NH₂ / KOH in Ethylene Glycol, Δ (Wolff-Kishner Reduction)
options.explanation: Basic deoxygenation of carbonyls to methylene groups.
Reduces >C=O to Alcohol (>CH-OH), not methylene (>CH₂).
PCC is an oxidizing agent.

solutionExplanation:
• A and B are correct: Clemmensen (Zn-Hg/HCl) and Wolff-Kishner (NH₂NH₂/KOH) convert >C=O into >CH₂.
• C is incorrect: LiAlH₄ reduces >C=O to an Alcohol (>CH-OH), NOT a hydrocarbon.
• D is incorrect: PCC is an oxidizing agent.
hints: Clemmensen and Wolff-Kishner both perform complete deoxygenation.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the valid statements regarding the Acidity of Carboxylic Acids: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than phenols because the negative charge on carboxylate (R-COO⁻) is delocalized equally over two electronegative oxygen atoms.
options.explanation: Equivalent resonance canonicals on electronegative oxygens maximize stability.

options.text: Electron-withdrawing groups (-I / -M) like -NO₂, -F, -Cl increase carboxylic acid strength.
options.explanation: EWG stabilizes the negative charge on carboxylate.

options.text: Almost all o-substituted benzoic acids are stronger acids than benzoic acid due to the Ortho-Effect.
options.explanation: Steric inhibition of resonance (SIR) forces -COOH out of plane, stabilizing carboxylate.

options.text: Acetic acid (CH₃COOH) is a stronger acid than Formic acid (HCOOH).
options.explanation: Formic acid (pKa 3.75) is stronger than Acetic acid (pKa 4.76) due to absence of +I methyl group.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Carboxylate resonance delocalizes charge over 2 oxygens; -I/-M groups increase acidity; o-substituted benzoic acids show the Ortho-Effect.
• D is incorrect: Formic acid (HCOOH, pK_a = 3.75) is STRONGER than Acetic acid (CH₃COOH, pK_a = 4.76) because the +I methyl group destabilizes the acetate anion.
hints: +I methyl group in acetic acid weakens acidity relative to formic acid.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following compounds will give a POSITIVE IODOFORM TEST (CHI₃ ↓ yellow precipitate) when treated with Iodine and aqueous NaOH? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Contains CH₃CO- group (only aldehyde giving iodoform).
Methyl ketone giving positive iodoform test.
Methyl ketone giving positive iodoform test.
Lacks CH₃CO- methyl group, gives negative iodoform test.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO), Acetone (CH₃COCH₃), and Acetophenone (C₆H₅COCH₃) all contain the required CH₃CO- methyl ketone group.
• D is incorrect: Benzophenone (Ph-CO-Ph) lacks a methyl group attached to carbonyl and gives a negative iodoform test.
hints: Only compounds with a CH₃CO- or CH₃CH(OH)- group give a positive iodoform test.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following specific methods can be used to synthesize BENZALDEHYDE (C₆H₅CHO)? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Etard Reaction (Toluene + CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂ followed by H₃O⁺)
options.explanation: Chromyl chloride oxidation of toluene gives benzaldehyde.

options.text: Gattermann-Koch Reaction (Benzene + CO + HCl in anhyd. AlCl₃ / CuCl)
options.explanation: Direct formylation of benzene gives benzaldehyde.

options.text: Rosenmund Reduction of Benzoyl Chloride (C₆H₅COCl + H₂ / Pd-BaSO₄)
options.explanation: Catalytic reduction of benzoyl chloride gives benzaldehyde.
Reimer-Tiemann of phenol yields Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde), not benzaldehyde.

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Etard reaction, Gattermann-Koch, and Rosenmund reduction of benzoyl chloride are established syntheses of Benzaldehyde.
• D is incorrect: Reimer-Tiemann reaction of phenol yields Salicylaldehyde (2-Hydroxybenzaldehyde), NOT benzaldehyde.
hints: Reimer-Tiemann formylates phenol to salicylaldehyde.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the correct options regarding the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) Reaction: (Select all that apply)

options.text: Converts carboxylic acids possessing α-hydrogens into α-halo carboxylic acids.
options.explanation: Core reaction outcome.

options.text: Uses Chlorine or Bromine in the presence of Red Phosphorus (X₂ / Red P) followed by water.
options.explanation: Standard reagents.

options.text: Formic Acid (HCOOH) and Trimethylacetic acid (CH₃)₃C-COOH FAIL the HVZ reaction.
options.explanation: Both lack α-hydrogens.

options.text: It operates via an enol/acid halide intermediate.
options.explanation: PX₃ generates acid halide which enolizes readily.

solutionExplanation: All four options represent true chemical facts regarding the HVZ α-halogenation reaction and its requirement for α-hydrogens.
hints: HVZ requires at least one α-hydrogen to form the enol intermediate.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Acid Derivative Hydrolysis to Carboxylic Acid
questionText: Which of the following acid derivatives undergo conversion back to the parent Carboxylic Acid (RCOOH) upon nucleophilic acyl substitution / hydrolysis with water? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: RCOCl + H₂O ──► RCOOH + HCl.
(RCO)₂O + H₂O ──► 2 RCOOH.
RCOOR' + H₂O ──► RCOOH + R'OH.
RCONH₂ + H₂O ──► RCOOH + NH₃.

solutionExplanation: All four major acid derivatives (acyl chlorides, anhydrides, esters, amides) undergo nucleophilic acyl substitution upon hydrolysis (H₃O⁺) to regenerate the parent Carboxylic Acid (RCOOH).
hints: All four acid derivatives hydrolyze to carboxylic acids.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Select the correct statements regarding the reactivity of Carbonyls toward Nucleophilic Addition (A_N): (Select all that apply)

options.text: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than Ketones due to steric and electronic factors.
options.explanation: Aldehydes have less steric crowding and less +I stabilization.

options.text: Formaldehyde (HCHO) is the most reactive simple carbonyl compound.
options.explanation: No +I alkyl groups and minimal steric hindrance.

options.text: Electron-withdrawing groups (-I / -M) on an aromatic ring increase the reactivity of benzaldehydes toward nucleophiles.
options.explanation: EWG increases the δ+ electrophilic charge on the carbonyl carbon.

options.text: Propanone (Acetone) is more reactive than Ethanal (Acetaldehyde).
options.explanation: Ethanal (aldehyde) is MORE reactive than Propanone (ketone).

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Aldehydes > Ketones; HCHO is most reactive; -I/-M groups increase carbonyl electrophilicity.
• D is incorrect: Ethanal (CH₃CHO, aldehyde) is MORE reactive than Propanone (CH₃COCH₃, ketone).
hints: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones due to steric and electronic factors.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following reagents can be used to convert an Acid Chloride (RCOCl) into a Ketone (R-CO-R')? (Select all that apply)

options.explanation: Reacts with acid chlorides to yield ketones without reacting further with the ketone.
Gilman reagent selectively couples with acid chlorides to give ketones.

options.text: Grignard Reagent (R'MgX) in 1:1 stoichiometric ratio under controlled conditions
options.explanation: Controlled low-temperature reaction can isolate the ketone.
Concentrated NaOH hydrolyzes acid chlorides to carboxylate salts (RCOONa).

solutionExplanation:
• A, B, C are correct: Dialkylcadmium (R'₂Cd), Gilman reagents (R'₂CuLi), and controlled Grignard reagents convert acid chlorides into ketones.
• D is incorrect: Concentrated NaOH hydrolyzes acid chlorides to carboxylate salts (RCOONa).
hints: Organocadmium and Gilman reagents are milder than Grignards and selectively stop at ketones.
